author: RACE ARCHIBALD
title: STATE GOLF: 6A and 5A tournaments return to Treasure Valley - NewsBreak
text:
By RACE ARCHIBALD ,
16 hours ago
For the first time since the spring of 2022, the last time Idaho’s top classifications in golf competed in the spring, the state golf tournaments are back in the Treasure Valley.
The 6A boys and girls golf state tournaments begin Thursday at RedHawk Golf Course in Nampa. The championship round is Friday.
Local schools have dominated the state competition in recent history. The last non-Treasure Valley school — for both boys and girls — to win a team state title was the Highland girls team in 2017.
The Rocky Mountain girls team has won the last four state titles and is in line to capture a fifth in a row. The Grizzlies won the district championship last week at River Birch Golf Course in Star, led by Maggie Urian, who paced the field with a score of 77, winning by two strokes. Rocky Mountain had four golfers place inside the top 10. Urian placed fourth at the state tournament last year, six strokes behind the winner.
Borah, Eagle and Mountain View also qualified as teams due to their top-four finishes at the district tournament. Boise, Centennial, Owyhee and Ridgevue will also be represented in the tournament with individual qualifiers.
On the boys’ side, Mountain View finished atop the leaderboard at the district tournament by a single stroke over Boise, the defending state champion. Boise’s Reid Hoppock won the tournament by three strokes over Mountain View’s Mason McGee.
Hoppock finished tied for eighth at the state tournament last season, shooting +7. The Brave have won the last two state titles.
Eagle and Timberline also qualified as a team, while Centennial, Meridian and Owyhee had individual golfers qualify.
BISHOP KELLY EYES ANOTHER SWEEPThe 5A boys and girls state golf tournaments begin Friday at Purple Sage Golf Course in Caldwell, with the championship round on Saturday.
The Knights have won both boys and girls team titles the last two seasons and have the pieces to sweep once again. They swept the team titles at the district tournament last week at Scotch Pines Golf Course in Payette. Two-time defending state champion Cara Carter is positioned well for a third state title in a row after an individual title last week, finishing 14 strokes ahead of second place.
The Bishop Kelly boys took all three top spots in the individual leaderboard to fuel their win. Aidan Szentanai was the top finisher, three strokes ahead of teammate Charlie Hilvers. Szentanai finished third at the state tournament last season, Hilvers was fourth. The boys will go for a fourth state title in a row.
Middleton finished second in both the boys and girls tournaments to qualify for state. The Skyview boys qualified for state with a third-place finish.
